messages:
Ravi: Quick note from today's multi-region drill: when eu-west warmed down we saw resident writes stall because consent checks to the escrow service timed out. Suggest a small protocol: accept-local-with-flag -> emit escrow-token -> background-reconcile. Thoughts?

Tess: Sounds reasonable. We should avoid silent data loss. If we accept-local, mark object as "pending-consent" and ensure reads either hide PII or return a consent-required error.

Marco: Implementation idea: dataplane header X-Consent-Mode: accept-local|hold|deny. Control-plane per-tenant sets default. Dataplane will attach escrow-token header for background replay.

Ivy: Ops: need visibility in Console to see number of pending-consent objects per-tenant and per-region. Also alert if pending count > threshold for > 1h.

Ravi: Security: escrow-token should be short-lived and signed by control-plane, stored encrypted in region. Reconcile worker must validate signature and KMS unwrap before final write.

Tess: Edge-case: concurrent writes from two regions -> dedupe via X-Write-Nonce header. If conflict, control-plane picks authoritative based on region-priority or timestamp. Documented fallback.

Marco: For rollout: feature-flag, per-tenant opt-in, start with non-PII tenants. Add chaos test that simulates escrow latency and region cutover.

ops-bot: Canary scheduled for consent-replay-canary-2 at 2024-06-10T02:00Z. Will post results.

Ivy: Action items:
- Marco: draft dataplane header contract + dedupe rules (due Thu)
- Tess: prototyping reconcile worker and token validation (due Fri)
- Ravi: Console metrics mock + alerting thresholds (due Mon)

Ravi: Agreement check: react :thumbsup: to proceed with prototype.
